section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section introduces the apparent redundancy in the verse about dwelling in sukkot and the paradoxical requirement that the sukkah be both a permanent dwelling and a temporary structure.
section.t: "In sukkot you shall dwell for seven days; every citizen in Israel shall dwell in sukkot."
And the precise points of our Nesi'im regarding this are known.
For it is necessary to understand what is the duplication of the matter,
that after it already commands "in sukkot you shall dwell for seven days"
[this being a command to all of Israel and to each individual Jew]
what does it add further by saying "every citizen in Israel shall dwell in sukkot"?
Also, it is necessary to understand the very essence of the mitzvah of sukkah,
for seemingly it contains a contradiction.
For the sitting in the sukkah must be "you shall dwell" as in "you shall reside,"
for all seven days a person makes his sukkah permanent and his house temporary.
That just as during the entire year he dwells in his residence in a permanent manner,
conducting all his affairs there,
so too must be the manner of his sitting in the sukkah,
that he should conduct all his affairs in the sukkah,
and see that the sukkah is his residence and permanent place during these seven days.
However, together with this,
the actual construction of the sukkah is a temporary construction.
For this matter, that the sukkah must be a temporary structure, is a fundamental condition of the mitzvah,
and therefore a sukkah that is higher than twenty cubits is invalid.
For one of the reasons for this is that up to twenty cubits, one's dwelling is a temporary dwelling,
above twenty cubits, one's dwelling is not a temporary dwelling but a permanent dwelling,
and the sukkah must specifically be a temporary dwelling.
Nevertheless, for the seven days the sitting in it must be permanent,
which is seemingly a contradiction.
Now, in the mitzvah of sukkah there is another unique matter requiring explanation,
that the mitzvah of sukkah is a positive time-bound commandment,
and in addition to this, the mitzvah of sukkah is limited by the limitation of time,
it is also limited by the limitation of place,
that the place must be a fit place for making the sukkah.
For one who makes his sukkah under a tree, it is as if he made it inside a house,
for this is not a fit place for this mitzvah.
This is unlike other Festivals, where we find a limitation only regarding time, but we do not find that there is also a limitation regarding place.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section discusses the connection between the mitzvah of dwelling in the sukkah and the mitzvah of taking the Four Species, and questions why these specific four species were chosen.
section.t: b)
Now, following the mitzvah of sitting in the sukkah
("in sukkot you shall dwell")
comes the mitzvah of taking the Four Species,
as it is stated,
"And you shall take for yourselves on the first day, the fruit of a beautiful tree, branches of date palms, and a branch of a thick tree, and willows of the brook," etc.
[For the mitzvah of sitting in the sukkah is from the first moment at the beginning of the seven days of Sukkot,
and after this
(and following it),
in the morning
(at dawn,
and ideally at sunrise)
the time of obligation for the mitzvah of taking the Four Species begins,
for its mitzvah is specifically by day].
From this it is understood that the mitzvah of taking the Four Species has a connection to the matter of the sukkah.
And particularly according to what is known,
that the optimal mitzvah is that the taking of the Four Species should specifically be in the sukkah,
for by this it is further emphasized that there is a connection between the mitzvah of taking the Four Species
("and you shall take for yourselves")
and the mitzvah of sukkah
("in sukkot you shall dwell").
And it requires explanation,
what is the connection between these two mitzvot.
And particularly since seemingly they are separate mitzvot,
for the mitzvah of sukkah is for seven days,
unlike the mitzvah of taking the Four Species, the essence of the mitzvah and from the Torah is only on the first day.
[And further known is the distinction in this between the Temple and the outlying areas,
as explained in the Gemara,
the enactment of Rabban Yochanan ben Zakkai.
From this branch several laws and details of laws that apply even in our time, regarding the distinction between the first day and the six days after it.]
Now, regarding the Four Species themselves, it is necessary to understand,
why specifically these four species were chosen.
For although all of them are of the plant type, nevertheless, from the very beginning of the command it is emphasized that they must specifically be unique species.
And the species must all be in a manner of beauty,
as it is stated, "And you shall take for yourselves... the fruit of a beautiful tree," etc.,
and the Gemara expounded
that this also applies to the three species that follow
[even though in the verse "beautiful" is explicitly mentioned only regarding the etrog,
the first species].

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the mitzvot were given to refine the creations, and that the service of Sukkot is the cause for reaching the service of Shemini Atzeret.
section.t: c)
Now,
in addition to the above precise points, it is known from the saying of our Sages,
that the mitzvot were not given to Israel except to refine the creations through them
(as explained in many places).
For in addition to the essence of the mitzvah,
whose matter is that He sanctified us with His mitzvot and commanded us, and it must be fulfilled in order to fulfill the command and will of the Commander,
nevertheless, in addition to this, there is in the mitzvah a unique service and effect regarding the service of man in general.
And so it is regarding the service of Israel on the festival of Sukkot,
both in the mitzvah of "in sukkot you shall dwell for seven days,"
and regarding the mitzvah of "and you shall take for yourselves on the first day," etc.,
and in the Simchat Beit HaShoevah that follows,
that in all of them there is their matter and their effect in service,
to refine the creations through them.
And so it is also regarding the eighth day, Shemini Atzeret.
And although Shemini is a festival in its own right,
nevertheless, it is called "the eighth day,"
which itself indicates its connection to the seven days of Sukkot that precede it.
And furthermore,
(not only is Shemini Atzeret connected to Sukkot, but moreover)
that just as simply, in order to reach the eighth, seven days are required beforehand,
so too is it in their spiritual content of Sukkot and Shemini Atzeret,
that even though the service of Shemini Atzeret and Simchat Torah comes after
[i.e., it is higher than]
the service of the days of Sukkot that precede it,
nevertheless, the cause and factor for reaching the service of Shemini Atzeret is specifically the service of the seven days that precede it.
And from this is understood the superiority in the service of Sukkot,
that it is specifically the cause and factor
through which one comes to the service, the effluences, and the levels of the matter of Shemini Atzeret.
